en: Your forearm acts as a third-class lever when you lift a cup, where your elbow is the fulcrum and your bicep provides the effort.
Space shuttles use special heat shields to protect against the immense friction and air resistance generated when reentering Earth's atmosphere at high speeds.
Because the Moon's gravity is only one-sixth of Earth's, a person weighing sixty kilograms on Earth would weigh just ten kilograms on the Moon.
Earth's magnetic field acts like a giant invisible shield, deflecting harmful charged particles from the Sun away from our atmosphere.
Lightning is a massive discharge of static electricity, heating the surrounding air to thirty thousand degrees Celsius, which is five times hotter than the Sun's surface.
Because light travels at three hundred thousand kilometers per second, the sunlight you see actually left the Sun eight minutes ago.
Sound waves travel about four times faster in water than in air, which is why whales can communicate across vast ocean distances.
Water is unusual because it expands when it freezes, making ice less dense than liquid water, which is why ice cubes float in your glass.
A roller coaster's motor only pulls the cars up the first hill, using gravity to convert potential energy into kinetic energy for the rest of the ride.
A screw is actually an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder, which is why turning it requires less force than pushing it straight into wood.
An electromagnet only works when electric current flows through it, allowing junkyard cranes to pick up and instantly drop heavy metal cars.
When you rub your hands together, friction converts your kinetic energy into thermal energy, which is why your hands feel warm on a cold day.
